extracted.intended_audience: chief communications officers, senior public relations and corporate communications executives, and corporate leaders interested in communications strategy
extracted.subtask_description: Framework and pragmatic actions for CCOs to define and activate a company's unique corporate character and to build advocacy among stakeholders. The model describes a four-stage, behavioral-science–grounded process for turning awareness into advocacy at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define and activate corporate character
rubrics_metrics.description: CCOs can define and activate their companies' unique corporate character as the foundation for communications and advocacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report describes a new framework for how chief communications officers (CCOs) can define and activate their companies' unique corporate character and build “advocacy at scale." It provides a process for activating every organization's unique and differentiating character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forge shared belief (Belief)
rubrics_metrics.description: Move beyond mere awareness to forge shared belief with decision-makers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Belief: Moving beyond “awareness" to forge shared belief with decision-makers. The model emphasizes creating shared beliefs with vital stakeholders as the first stage of engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translate belief into action (Action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Convert forged belief into concrete actions by stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action: Translating belief into action – for example, to buy a product, invest in a company or accept a job offer. The framework focuses on turning belief into tangible behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convert success into ongoing behavior (Confidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinforce initial actions so stakeholders repeat and sustain the behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confidence: Translating success from one's actions into ongoing behavior. This stage is about turning a one-time action into continued behavior through reinforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale advocacy (Advocacy at Scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Turn changed behavior into active, broad-based advocacy on behalf of the shared agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocacy at Scale: Turning changed behavior into active advocacy on behalf of the now-shared agenda. The ultimate aim is to mobilize stakeholders as advocates across networks and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage diverse stakeholders as advocates
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage customers, investors, employees and community members as advocates for shared beliefs and actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report proposes methods for engaging individuals – whether customers, investors, employees or community members – as advocates for a set of shared beliefs and actions. Examples highlight different stakeholder types to target.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use a behavioral-science–grounded four-stage method
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a four-stage engagement method derived from modern behavioral science to build advocacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The new model's method for building advocacy grounded in corporate character is based on four stages of engagement, as identified by modern behavioral science. This implies using evidence-based behavioral techniques across the stages: belief, action, confidence, advocacy at scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt CCO role to the changing communications landscape
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernize the CCO's framework and approaches in response to shifts in how people communicate and form opinions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Business leaders face change at every turn – from newly empowered consumers and employees, to different ways of accessing information, to new levels of transparency. The report argues that CCOs need a new framework that reflects these new realities and can turn challenges into opportunities for enterprise success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground strategy in practitioner insight and pragmatic actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Base the model on practitioner surveys and provide pragmatic, actionable steps for implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report, in part, is the result of a survey of chief communications officers from such companies as Johnson & Johnson, P&G, Apple, eBay, Pepsico, FedEx and IBM about how their roles and functions are changing. It outlines pragmatic actions for succeeding in today's radically changing business environment.
